title: AI 要跨越盧比孔河了嗎？自我成長的 AI 離我們多遠 (下集)

topic_alignment.paraphrase: Lee asks whether changing an agent’s harness can impair an old skill even when its parameters stay fixed. He introduces the May paper at 1832.030 seconds.

Lee explains the three rounds and the vertical code-length axis of the left panel. He introduces the retention constraints at 1899.330 seconds and turns to the two models in the right panel at 1923.588 seconds.
Lee observes that successive agents may change under a fixed rule for producing the next update. He asks at 2020.318 seconds whether that rule can change too.

Lee returns to updating a harness. Starting at 2048.813 seconds his example reads existing code and benchmark feedback before proposing a replacement. The cue starts a discussion spanning the next slides.
Lee qualifies the self-editing example. Many systems that update harnesses use a fixed improvement module, sometimes an external model. The diagram identifies the update role with the wrench symbol.
